findings: An infiltrative pancreatic cancer measuring 55 mm is observed in the body of the pancreas. Serosal invasion and retropancreatic tissue invasion are noted. The tumor is in contact with the aorta, with an indistinct boundary, suggesting invasion. No other local invasion factors are identified. Lymph node metastasis is observed in one node at station 9. No other metastases are observed.

responses.content:
Task 1: Diagnose the local invasion factors of pancreatic cancer.

CH0 (no invasion of the common hepatic duct)
DU0 (no invasion of the duodenum)
S1 (serosal invasion)
RP1 (retropancreatic tissue invasion)
PV0 (no invasion of the portal vein)
A1 (invasion of the aorta)
PL0 (no invasion of the pancreatic lymphatic vessels)
OO1 (invasion of the omentum)

Task 2: Determine the classification for local invasion (T classification) of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the size of the tumor (55 mm) and the presence of serosal invasion, retropancreatic tissue invasion, and invasion of the aorta, the T classification is T3.

Task 3: Determine the N classification of pancreatic cancer.

Regional lymph nodes for pancreatic cancer in the body of the pancreas are:
- Station 8 (celiac lymph nodes)
- Station 9 (suprapancreatic lymph nodes)
- Station 10 (pancreaticoduodenal lymph nodes)
- Station 11 (transverse pancreatic lymph nodes)
- Station 12 (parapancreatic lymph nodes)

The patient's metastatic lymph node station is:
- Station 9 (suprapancreatic lymph nodes)

Since there is only one metastatic lymph node at station 9, the N classification is N1a.

Task 4: Determine the M classification of pancreatic cancer.

There are no distant metastases, so the M classification is M0.

Task 5: Determine the resectability classification of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the results of Task 1 and Task 4, the tumor is resectable because there is no evidence of distant or non-regional metastasis, and the local invasion factors do not meet the criteria for borderline resectable or unresectable.

Task 6: Determine the overall stage according to the JPS staging system.

Based on the T classification (T3), N classification (N1a), and M classification (M0), the overall stage is Stage IIA.
